lastVerifiedRecord.description: Expected Outcome: A consolidated reference on private situational data relevant for submarine-cable security A structured description of the main categories of private situational data and actors relevant for submarine-cable security, including their sensitivity profile, typical usage, and the key legal, regulatory and commercial constraints affecting possible access by Regional Cable Hubs. Interoperability and data fusion pathways for multi-source, multi-basin use Clear conclusions on the main interoperability and data fusion challenges and feasible solutions (e.g. common data models or ontologies, interoperability layers, translation and fusion layers), including indications on which approaches are realistically applicable across multiple providers and sea basins, and how they can remain extensible to accommodate new data sources and actors over time. A proof-of-concept demonstration showing how selected private situational data can be accessed, integrated and processed within a Regional Cable Hub–type environment, together with a practical demonstration of the situational-awareness outcomes that such integration can produce. This includes evidence on the achievable levels of spatial precision, timeliness, coverage and reliability under pilot conditions, as well as identification of the constraints that limit performance. Partnership models and recommendations for EU follow-up A concise set of partnership models through which Regional Cable Hubs could obtain or use private situational data (e.g. service-based, data-sharing, or hybrid arrangements), with associated requirements for their viability and compliance, an assessment of their expected impact and limitations on situational awareness, and recommendations for possible EU-level guidance, support measures or follow-up actions. Objective: The situational data that could contribute to improved awareness of threats to submarine cables (e.g. sensor feeds, maritime or satellite surveillance data) are subject to complex and heterogeneous governance conditions . These conditions may vary across cable systems, operators and sea basins, reflecting differing ownership structures, contractual arrangements and applicable regulatory or security frameworks. As a result, there is currently limited clarity on how such data could be accessed, combined and used in a structured manner to support cable-security objectives. The Pilot Project aims , through analytical work and targeted pilot activities in non-operational settings, to determine how private-sector situational data relevant to submarine-cable security could support the functioning of Regional Cable Hubs, as envisaged under the EU Action Plan on Cable Security and currently under implementation at Union level (established under the Digital Europe Programme (DEP) Call 9). In view of the preparatory nature of the action, proposals are encouraged to build on relevant experience and capacities developed in related Union initiatives on submarine cable security, including by entities involved in the establishment of Regional Cable Hubs. Scope: The Pilot Project will combine interaction with the range of concerned private actors related to cable security and analysis with small-scale pilots to explore the full process of accessing and using such data: Map the landscape of situational data held by private actors relevant to submarine-cable security , sources and type of such data (cable-related telemetry, sensor feeds, satellite and maritime-surveillance data, underwater-drone outputs and other emerging modalities); identify their technical characteristics (e.g. real-time, proprietary formats, latency, frequency), ownership, confidentiality profile, availability, usage patterns and the legal, contractual, security or other applicable constraints governing their access. Assess the feasibility of accessing and integrating such data into a Regional Cable Hub , by first examining the commercial, organisational, regulatory and security conditions under which private actors could interface with Cable Hubs, and then analysing the technical implications of such cooperation, including the requirements for data ingestion (such as APIs, gateways, pipelines, authentication and security controls) and the maturity and limitations of existing commercial or open platforms that could support this integration and subsequent data fusion. Analyse interoperability and data fusion challenges across multiple providers, diverse data sources and different sea basins , including whether harmonisation of formats, frequencies and semantics is needed; the potential role of common data models, taxonomies or ontologies; the feasibility of using interoperability and fusion layers; and how these approaches could remain future-proof in light of evolving sensors and emerging sources of data; and finally how interoperable data can be fused to generate coherent situational awareness. Assess the quality and limitations of the situational awareness generated from these data sources. Determine the realistic contribution that private-sector monitoring and situational data can make to submarine-cable security by evaluating the spatial precision, timeliness, coverage, reliability and confidence that can be achieved when such data is combined within a Regional Cable Hub, while also identifying the technical, regulatory and commercial limitations that constrain the level of situational awareness attainable under different data-access and integration scenarios. Design and carry out pilot or proof-of-concept demonstrations (e.g. using sample datasets, synthetic data or sandbox integrations with selected providers) to test and validate key assumptions on data access, integration, interoperability and situational-awareness outputs, and to refine the practical feasibility of the proposed cooperation models. Produce a consolidated assessment of feasible partnership models between Regional Cable Hubs and private holders of cable-relevant monitoring and situational data, setting out the key commercial, contractual, technical and regulatory requirements for such arrangements, evaluate the extent to which they can enhance the situational awareness achievable for submarine-cable security, and identify gaps where further EU-level policy guidance, standardisation or supporting measures may be needed.

title: Integrated Surveillance mechanism: Regional Cable hubs
callTitle: Integrated Surveillance mechanism: Regional Cable hubs
descriptionByte:
Expected Outcome:

  • A consolidated reference on private situational data relevant for submarine-cable security
    A structured description of the main categories of private situational data and actors relevant for submarine-cable security, including their sensitivity profile, typical usage, and the key legal, regulatory and commercial constraints affecting possible access by Regional Cable Hubs.

  • Interoperability and data fusion pathways for multi-source, multi-basin use
    Clear conclusions on the main interoperability and data fusion challenges and feasible solutions (e.g. common data models or ontologies, interoperability layers, translation and fusion layers), including indications on which approaches are realistically applicable across multiple providers and sea basins, and how they can remain extensible to accommodate new data sources and actors over time.

  • A proof-of-concept demonstration showing how selected private situational data can be accessed, integrated and processed within a Regional Cable Hub–type environment, together with a practical demonstration of the situational-awareness outcomes that such integration can produce. This includes evidence on the achievable levels of spatial precision, timeliness, coverage and reliability under pilot conditions, as well as identification of the constraints that limit performance.

  • Partnership models and recommendations for EU follow-up
    A concise set of partnership models through which Regional Cable Hubs could obtain or use private situational data (e.g. service-based, data-sharing, or hybrid arrangements), with associated requirements for their viability and compliance, an assessment of their expected impact and limitations on situational awareness, and recommendations for possible EU-level guidance, support measures or follow-up actions.

Objective:

The situational data that could contribute to improved awareness of threats to submarine cables (e.g. sensor feeds, maritime or satellite surveillance data) are subject to complex and heterogeneous governance conditions. These conditions may vary across cable systems, operators and sea basins, reflecting differing ownership structures, contractual arrangements and applicable regulatory or security frameworks. As a result, there is currently limited clarity on how such data could be accessed, combined and used in a structured manner to support cable-security objectives.

The Pilot Project aims, through analytical work and targeted pilot activities in non-operational settings, to determine how private-sector situational data relevant to submarine-cable security could support the functioning of Regional Cable Hubs, as envisaged under the EU Action Plan on Cable Security and currently under implementation at Union level (established under the Digital Europe Programme (DEP) Call 9).

In view of the preparatory nature of the action, proposals are encouraged to build on relevant experience and capacities developed in related Union initiatives on submarine cable security, including by entities involved in the establishment of Regional Cable Hubs.

Scope:

The Pilot Project will combine interaction with the range of concerned private actors related to cable security and analysis with small-scale pilots to explore the full process of accessing and using such data:

  • Map the landscape of situational data held by private actors relevant to submarine-cable security, sources and type of such data (cable-related telemetry, sensor feeds, satellite and maritime-surveillance data, underwater-drone outputs and other emerging modalities); identify their technical characteristics (e.g. real-time, proprietary formats, latency, frequency), ownership, confidentiality profile, availability, usage patterns and the legal, contractual, security or other applicable constraints governing their access.
  • Assess the feasibility of accessing and integrating such data into a Regional Cable Hub, by first examining the commercial, organisational, regulatory and security conditions under which private actors could interface with Cable Hubs, and then analysing the technical implications of such cooperation, including the requirements for data ingestion (such as APIs, gateways, pipelines, authentication and security controls) and the maturity and limitations of existing commercial or open platforms that could support this integration and subsequent data fusion.
  • Analyse interoperability and data fusion challenges across multiple providers, diverse data sources and different sea basins, including whether harmonisation of formats, frequencies and semantics is needed; the potential role of common data models, taxonomies or ontologies; the feasibility of using interoperability and fusion layers; and how these approaches could remain future-proof in light of evolving sensors and emerging sources of data; and finally how interoperable data can be fused to generate coherent situational awareness.
  • Assess the quality and limitations of the situational awareness generated from these data sources. Determine the realistic contribution that private-sector monitoring and situational data can make to submarine-cable security by evaluating the spatial precision, timeliness, coverage, reliability and confidence that can be achieved when such data is combined within a Regional Cable Hub, while also identifying the technical, regulatory and commercial limitations that constrain the level of situational awareness attainable under different data-access and integration scenarios.
  • Design and carry out pilot or proof-of-concept demonstrations (e.g. using sample datasets, synthetic data or sandbox integrations with selected providers) to test and validate key assumptions on data access, integration, interoperability and situational-awareness outputs, and to refine the practical feasibility of the proposed cooperation models.
  • Produce a consolidated assessment of feasible partnership models between Regional Cable Hubs and private holders of cable-relevant monitoring and situational data, setting out the key commercial, contractual, technical and regulatory requirements for such arrangements, evaluate the extent to which they can enhance the situational awareness achievable for submarine-cable security, and identify gaps where further EU-level policy guidance, standardisation or supporting measures may be needed.

Maximum price for ESA: EUR 70,000 with a minimum company co-funding of EUR 10,000. To be published in the Open Space Innovation Platform (OSIP, https://ideas.esa.int/): Type H  Space Related Training Courses, for the cost reimbursement of participation of employees in space related training courses. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 9,999. More information and further programmatic constraints can be consulted in the cover letter of the call upon its issue date.

Details Unlocking Space for Business The UK Space Agency’s Unlocking Space for Business (USB) programme is seeking to accelerate the adoption of space-enabled data and services to address environmental intelligence and emissions challenges across the UK economy. This challenge-led competition is designed to support projects that demonstrate how space-enabled data, technologies and services can help organisations improve environmental monitoring, emissions measurement, reporting and verification, and wider environmental decision-making. The competition aims to stimulate greater collaboration between end users, data integrators and space-sector suppliers, while supporting the development of solutions with credible pathways to future operational adoption. Who can apply This competition is open to UK-registered end-user businesses, including SMEs, leading a consortium with at least one UK space supplier and any additional integrator or delivery partner organisations required to support project delivery. For the purposes of this competition, end-user businesses are organisations that use space-enabled products, services or insights to address operational challenges, improve decision-making, manage risk or deliver commercial outcomes. The competition is particularly aimed at end-user organisations operating in sectors including financial services, insurance, asset management, energy, utilities, infrastructure, agriculture, land management and environmental services. Applications from organisations in other sectors are also welcome, provided they can demonstrate a clear environmental intelligence or emissions-related use case aligned with the competition objectives. The UK Space Agency invites applications from end-user-led consortia comprising: An end-user organisation seeking to address one of the competition’s environmental intelligence or emissions challenge statements At least one supplier of space-enabled data, products or services; and Any additional delivery partners or integrators required to support successful project delivery. Applicant webinar The UK Space Agency will host an applicant webinar on 3 November 2026, 11:00 GMT to provide an overview of the competition, explain the challenge statements, outline the application process and answer participant questions. Interested organisations are strongly encouraged to attend. Details of how to register can be found Unlocking Space for Business: Environmental Intelligence and Emissions Grant Call Briefing Webinar. Funding available The UK Space Agency intends to award up to £2 million through this competition. Applicants may request up to £400,000 grant funding per project. Total project costs may be higher where match funding is provided by consortium partners. In exceptional circumstances, the UK Space Agency reserves the right to adjust the total funding available, the number of projects funded, or the value of individual awards. Project duration Projects are expected to start in January 2027 and run for approximately 9 months. Projects must be sufficiently mature to demonstrate operational value within the funded period and deliver measurable outcomes by the end of the project. How to apply Applications must be submitted through the Flexigrant portal by 16:00 GMT on 11 December 2026. Applicants must complete all required sections of the online application form and upload the required supporting documentation through the Flexigrant platform which can be accessed here: Flexigrant . Applications submitted by email will not be accepted. Late applications will not be accepted. Your application must include: A completed application form; Annex A: Proposed Milestone Table Annex B: Project Cost Breakdown Annex C: National Security Questionnaire (where required) Any additional supporting documentation requested within the application process. Applicants should read the full competition guidance before submitting an application. Sign up for emails or print this page Get emails about this page Print this page

This interview, conducted in English, is a crucial step, allowing you to discuss your project in detail and answer any questions from the board. Ensure that you carefully prepare for the TEB interview by thoroughly understanding your proposal and being ready to discuss both the technical and business aspects in detail. TEB Decision & Certificate: Once the TEB has completed its evaluation and your interview, you will be formally notified of the outcome. If approved, ESA will issue your official TEB Selection Certificate, confirming your eligibility to secure the Junta de Andalucía’s co-financing approval prior to final contract signature. Detailed instructions for the co-financing application process follow. Contract Signing: Once the contract is signed, your startup officially begins its incubation period with ESA BIC Andalusia. Complete the non-competitive grant form as established in the Open Call documentation and the referenced Regulatory Bases, attach your TEB Selection Certificate and all required administrative documents, and submit through the official channel. Regional co-funding is awarded to projects that have passed the TEB evaluation and meet the formal eligibility requirements set out in the Open Call and Regulatory Bases. Applications are processed in order of validation and subject to budget availability. You will then be notified of the award decision. record.description: ApplyESA BIC Andalusia2026-10-29T15:23:31+01:00 Who Can ApplyEnsure your startup can join our incubation programme To be eligible for ESA BIC Andalusia, your startup or business idea must meet the following criteria: Space-Related InnovationYour business must have a solid connection to space-related technology, expertise, or applications. This connection can be categorized as either Downstream or Upstream: Downstream This involves the application or exploitation of space systems or technologies in non-space domains. Your business idea may focus on: Applications utilizing satellite navigation, earth observation, or satellite communication.Technology transfer involving space-related hardware, software, or intellectual property.Providing solutions that leverage space data or technology to innovate in other sectorsUpstream This relates to the development of new technologies intended for use within the space sector. Examples include: Developing new systems, subsystems, or components for space missions.Technologies and services designed for use on space missions or in human spaceflight activities.Your application must clearly justify the space connection, demonstrating how it advances or innovates within the space sector. It is crucial that the space connection is clear and justified in your application. For further guidance on ensuring your idea meets the necessary criteria, please consult the Space Connection Assessment document. This will help you evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea to meet the requirements set by ESA BIC Andalusia. Viable Business PlanYou must present a clear and viable business plan outlining your strategy for growth, the market potential of your product or service, and how your space-related innovation will be commercialized. The business plan should also detail financial projections, key milestones, and risk management strategies. Company AgeNew or existing companies less than 5 years old. If Your Company is Already Established Your startup must be legally registered in Spain and must not be older than five years at the time of application. If Your Company is Not Yet Established You are eligible to apply as an informal group of entrepreneurs, provided you commit to legally registering your startup in Andalusia upon acceptance into the programme. Company LocationYour business must be, or commit to being, located in Andalusia during the incubation period. ESA BIC Andalusia is strategically located in the Naves de Renfe building in the San Jerónimo district of Seville, near the Spanish Space Agency headquarters. Commitment to the programmeYour team must be fully committed to engaging with the ESA BIC Andalusia programme throughout the entire incubation period. This includes regular attendance at workshops, mentoring sessions, and events organized by the incubator, as well as making full use of the resources provided. How to ApplyFollow these steps and turn your ideas into successful businesses Check Your EligibilityEnsure your startup meets the eligibility criteria for ESA BIC Andalusia. If you are unsure, visit the Who can apply section for more information. Contact Our TeamIt is highly recommended to contact ESA BIC Andalusia in advance to inform us about your intention to apply. The team will assist you in determining whether your business idea is suitable for incubation and will explain what is needed from the applicant. Download The Application FormsAll application forms and supporting documents are available below. Download the full Application Package and submit your proposal. Download the Application Package (.zip)Prepare Your ApplicationBefore you begin filling out any forms, it is strongly recommended that you carefully read all the provided documents. Application Templates The Application Package contains the following documents: ESA BIC Andalusia Open Call (call conditions and process) ESA BIC Application Form (the document to complete and submit, including its annexes) Draft Incubation Contract Space Connection Assessment Supporting Documents Make sure to thoroughly review all supporting documents, particularly the Draft Incubation Contract. This document is crucial for understanding your contractual obligations and ensuring you are fully informed before proceeding with your application. Documents Preparation Application Form: complete all required sections following the instructions inside the form. It replaces the previous separate templates (cover letter, business plan and incubation proposal). Include details on how you intend to use the incentive funding. The form must be signed by the majority shareholder, or by shareholders jointly holding more than 50% of the shares; the signature also confirms acceptance of the Incubation Contract conditions. Draft Incubation Contract: read it carefully before applying. Modifications or amendments may only be considered in exceptional cases. Space Connection Assessment: use this document to evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea. Application SubmissionBefore submitting, review all your documents carefully. Ensure that each section is completed according to the instructions provided in the templates. Once everything is in order, submit the completed Application Form as a single PDF file to opencall-esabic-andalusia@catec.aero, with the subject ‘ESA BIC Andalusia Open Call’. Important: Ensure your submission is completed before the announced cut-off date. Submissions received after the cut-off deadline will not be considered for that particular round. Evaluation ProcessAfter submitting your application to ESA BIC Andalusia, the post-submission process is as follows: TOB Review: Your application first undergoes an initial screening by the Tender Opening Board (TOB). The TOB checks the completeness of your application and whether it meets the formal requirements. TEB Evaluation: If the TOB process is successful, your application is then forwarded to the Tender Evaluation Board (TEB). The TEB is composed of representatives from the European Space Agency (ESA), the Spanish Space Agency (AEE), ESA BIC Andalusia, the Junta de Andalucía as regional co-funder, and external experts. This board will conduct a detailed evaluation of your proposal, focusing on technical feasibility, business potential, and alignment with the goals of the ESA BIC programme. Interview with TEB: As part of the TEB evaluation, you will be invited to present your business idea. This interview, conducted in English, is a crucial step, allowing you to discuss your project in detail and answer any questions from the board. Ensure that you carefully prepare for the TEB interview by thoroughly understanding your proposal and being ready to discuss both the technical and business aspects in detail. TEB Decision & Certificate: Once the TEB has completed its evaluation and your interview, you will be formally notified of the outcome. If approved, ESA will issue your official TEB Selection Certificate, confirming your eligibility to secure the Junta de Andalucía’s co-financing approval prior to final contract signature. Detailed instructions for the co-financing application process follow. Contract Signing: Once the contract is signed, your startup officially begins its incubation period with ESA BIC Andalusia. Regional Co-Funding ApplicationAfter receiving your TEB Selection Certificate, you must submit your regional co-funding application via the Junta de Andalucía’s e-Office portal before the deadline indicated in the Call to secure co-funding from the regional authority. Complete the non-competitive grant form as established in the Open Call documentation and the referenced Regulatory Bases, attach your TEB Selection Certificate and all required administrative documents, and submit through the official channel. Regional co-funding is awarded to projects that have passed the TEB evaluation and meet the formal eligibility requirements set out in the Open Call and Regulatory Bases. Applications are processed in order of validation and subject to budget availability. You will then be notified of the award decision. Sign Contract & Start IncubationUpon confirmation of your regional co-funding, you will sign the Incubation Contract. With your signature in place, your incubation officially begins, granting you access to a comprehensive suite of programme services—high-level mentoring, state-of-the-art technical facilities, expert business coaching, dedicated legal & IPR support, the 60K € financing package, dynamic networking events, and community collaboration opportunities. Welcome aboard: incubation officially starts! Open Call for ProposalsESA BIC Andalusia operates under a continuous Open Call system, meaning that applications are accepted year-round. Proposals are evaluated at specific cut-off dates. Submissions are now closed Download the Application Package above and prepare your proposal to participate in the next evaluation round. Need Assistance?If you have any questions or require further clarification, please contact the ESA BIC Andalusia team directly. You are also encouraged to consult the FAQ for additional guidance and information. Contact the ESA BIC Andalusia teamConsult the Frequently Asked Questions
